audit.whatIsWrong: Two rows contradicted their own whys. Level 6 read Graves while whys[4] calls Nature's Grasp 'your hardest all-in and best kill window of the lane', and 2+ items read Maokai while whys[6] warns 'force it now, because once his shotgun and tank items come fully online he kites you and reclaims the duel' and spikes[3] calls late 'Graves' biggest threat window'.
audit.why: Level 6 genuinely is Maokai's — a 3000-range root is the one thing Quickdraw's 425-range dash cannot answer. Late genuinely is Graves'. Fixing both also settles packet.defects: the chart now reads 4/7 Maokai with the loss condition on the row the 45.56% win rate comes from.
audit.corrected: Level 6 to Maokai at 6/10, 2+ items to Graves at 4/10, proposed as matched full+content pairs in one group.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why and phases[6].why were boilerplate that named no spike.
audit.why: The two spikes that decide this lane are Nature's Grasp at 6 (3000 range vs a 425-range dash) and Graves' True Grit plus shotgun scaling at two items.
audit.corrected: Both rewritten with the real ranges and the resulting instruction — hold R for a gank at 6, stop duelling at two items.

audit.whatIsWrong: Smoke Screen is described as blinding in two places — wants.foe[1] says he drops it 'to blind your auto and break your Sap Magic heal proc', and spikes[3] says he 'blinds your auto with Smoke Screen'. Riot's text says it 'creates a cloud of smoke that reduces sight range' and slows on impact. It does not blind, and it cannot break an auto-attack proc.
audit.why: A player who believes Smoke Screen blinds him will stop auto-attacking inside it and give up free damage and free Sap Magic procs. It also does not stop a targeted Twisted Advance, which is the opposite of how the page reads.
audit.corrected: Corrected in wants.foe[1], spikes[3].text, mid and breakdown.cooldowns, each stating sight reduction and slow.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing mentioned that New Destiny fires four bullets that cannot pass through units.
audit.why: It is the single best free mitigation in the lane and it is Maokai-specific: standing so a minion is between you and Graves eats most of the shell. Nothing on the page told the player to do it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Quickdraw was tracked everywhere with no number, and nothing said his basic attacks lower its cooldown.
audit.why: 16s at rank 1 is a long window, but it shrinks every time he lands an auto — so 'don't let him free-hit you' is not a style note, it is what keeps the dash down.
audit.corrected: The 16s figure and the attack-refund written into breakdown.cooldowns, tradeGood and mid.

edits.before: Passive heal + AA trades carry the early waves. Identify how Graves contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: New Destiny fires 4 bullets that cannot pass through units — stand behind a minion and most of the shell misses you entirely.

edits.before: Nature’s Grasp roots whole teams — lane it only for kill windows. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Graves's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Level 6 is your window: Nature's Grasp is a 3000-range root he cannot Quickdraw out of. Hold it for a gank, not for chip damage.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Graves carry threat 8/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items on he reclaims it — shotgun damage plus True Grit armour out-DPS Sap Magic. Stop duelling and play him as a lockdown.

edits.before: - Graves Quickdraw: matchup-defining — His dash + armor stacks. Engage when it's down. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Graves Quickdraw: matchup-defining — 16s at rank 1, only 425 range, and his autos cut it shorter. Engage when it's down. - Smoke Screen: 26s at rank 1 — it hides him, it does not blind you. - Collateral Damage: 100s.

edits.before: W-root Graves the moment his answer is down, Q-knockback the follow-up, and let brush saplings tax his every path.
edits.after: W-root him once Quickdraw is spent — 16s at rank 1 — Q him past his 425 dash range, and sapling his kite path.

edits.before: Drop W (Smoke Screen) on himself to blind your auto and break your Sap Magic heal proc
edits.after: Drop W (Smoke Screen) to cut your sight of him and slow you so he can reset the distance

edits.before: Graves' biggest threat window: with shotgun damage and tank items he kites your cooldowns, blinds your auto with Smoke Screen, and out-DPSes your Sap Magic heal.
edits.after: Graves' biggest threat window: with shotgun damage and True Grit armour he kites your cooldowns, hides in Smoke Screen to break your chase, and out-DPSes Sap Magic.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are a coinflip on whether he respects your W; if he hugs minions to dodge it, you farm and wait. At 6 your R (Nature's Grasp) is the swing — it's a long brambles wave he can't reliably E out of, so you root him for a gank and that's where most of your kills come from. Bait his W (Smoke Screen): if he drops it to blind you, that's his self-peel gone, and your next W has no answer. Watch his True Grit — every auto he lands stacks armor, so don't let him free-hit you while you wait for cooldowns.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are a coinflip on whether he respects your W; if he hugs minions to dodge it, you farm and wait. At 6 your R (Nature's Grasp) is the swing — a 3000-range brambles wave he can't reliably E out of, so you root him for a gank and that's where most of your kills come from. Smoke Screen only cuts sight and slows, so it never stops a targeted W — but once he spends it his self-peel is gone. Watch True Grit: every auto he lands stacks armour and shortens his 16s dash.

notes: One thing worth flagging: whys[0] and the level-1 row disagree in tone — the row gives Graves level 1 (correct: he outranges you and you have one ability) while whys[0] spends most of its length on what happens at level 2. I left it alone because it is not false, only oddly framed. Also left alone deliberately: whether Graves' End of the Line detonating on terrain is triggered by Nature's Grasp's bramble wall. The kit derives a 'terrain' flag on both abilities but Riot's text does not say Maokai's wall is collision terrain, and guessing either way would be worse than the current silence.
